name: Shelf Patchwork Tank (Scavenged)
description:
Not a manufactured item — this is something built from nothing. A tank top assembled from three or four mismatched fabric sources: a section of old corporate uniform fabric (the logo partially burned or bleached out), a strip of fluorescent mesh from a construction vest, and a back panel that might be repurposed synth-bag material. Whoever made it knew what they were doing — the seams hold, the armholes are clean, and someone has added a hand-stitched border along the collar in a tight cross-stitch pattern using bright orange thread. Every one of these is unique.

On the Shelf, you wear what you can get. But there's craft here — real craft. Some of these tanks end up in Tier 3 boutiques with a four-hundred-quanta markup and a story about 'authentic street construction.' The people who made them don't see a coin of that.
what_it_says: You make do. You also make something out of making do — there's pride in this, even if the world doesn't see it that way.
worn_by: young people with nothing and style anyway
story_hooks: The burned-out logo on the front is from a corponation that was supposedly dissolved fifteen years ago — but someone is still making uniforms with that mark.
A Tier 4 fashion house has started producing 'authentic Shelf-inspired' reproductions of this style, and the backlash from Tier 1 communities is building toward something uglier than protest.
A character recognizes the cross-stitch pattern as a specific maker's signature — and that maker disappeared six months ago.
